# Copy for Originals Tools

> Small, free, single-purpose web tools for PPC marketers, copywriters and short-form video scriptwriters. Every tool runs entirely in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

## Tools

- [Keyword Triage: Google Ads keyword profitability checker](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/keyword-triage/): Reads a Google Ads or Microsoft Ads keyword report (CSV, TSV or .xlsx) and labels each keyword Cut, Trim bids, Keep, Scale or Needs data against a target CPA or ROAS. The page documents every rule, default threshold and formula the tool uses.
- [Negative Keyword Finder: Google Ads search terms analyzer](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/negative-keywords/): Reads a Google Ads or Microsoft Ads search terms report (CSV, TSV or .xlsx) and flags the search terms that break two limits you enter before uploading: an unacceptable cost per conversion, and a spend limit with no conversions. It also finds words shared across many search terms that spent past the spend limit without converting. Copies them as exact-match and phrase-match negative keywords. The page documents every rule, default and safeguard, including why it recommends 90 days of data.
- [Lead Gen Search Campaign Checklist](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/search-checklist/): An interactive preflight checklist for Google Ads lead gen Search campaigns covering account settings, campaign settings, bidding and budget, keywords and ads, and post-launch checks. Sets the minimum daily budget at 3× the target CPA.
- [Target CPA & ROAS Calculator](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/target-cpa-roas/): A step-by-step calculator for setting a Google Ads target CPA or target ROAS for the first time. Gross profit = average sale × gross margin. For lead gen, break-even CPA = gross profit × the share of leads that become customers, and target CPA = break-even CPA × the share of gross profit spent on ads; for ecommerce, break-even ROAS = 1 ÷ gross margin and target ROAS = 1 ÷ (gross margin × share). Because people overestimate how many leads close, it asks for a gut guess, then checks it against a count from records or a leak estimate (real leads × leads reached × close rate). Recommends a daily budget of 3× target CPA and moving an existing target 15% or less a week from today's cost per conversion or ROAS.
- [PPC Troubleshooter: Google Ads clicks but no conversions, not spending, or dropped](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/ppc-troubleshooter/): An interactive diagnosis tool for Google Ads campaigns that aren't working: clicks but no conversions, a budget used up by a few expensive clicks, conversions that suddenly dropped, a rising cost per click, or ads that barely show or spend. Asks follow-up questions one at a time and returns ranked causes and fixes. Every cause the tool can return is also written out in static text as cause → how it is spotted → what to do, for all five problems. Shows whether results are bad luck using the chance of zero conversions, (1 − conversion rate)^clicks, with a table by clicks (20 to 300) and conversion rate (1% to 10%); at 2.5%, zero from 100 clicks happens 8% of the time and from 200 clicks 1%. Luck drops under 5% at 3 ÷ conversion rate clicks (120 at 2.5%). Tests drops with a binomial test (likely luck at 10% or more). Sizes budgets from cost per click ÷ conversion rate, with a table of daily budget ($10 to $100) × cost per click ($2 to $50) → clicks a month and expected leads at 2.5% (for example $10 a day at $10 a click is 30 clicks and 0.8 leads a month). Maps Google's own status labels (Eligible (limited), Limited by bid strategy, Learning, Limited, Misconfigured, Below first page bid estimate, Low search volume, Under review, Disapproved, Needs attention, Awaiting conversions) to Google's definition and a fix. Also covers clicks but no phone calls, spam leads, and how long to wait (in clicks, not days). Asks for the advertiser's own cost per click rather than an industry average, and explains why: averages such as LocaliQ's $9.30 for personal injury mix every keyword and city, so they can be several times lower than what contested keywords cost. Lists LocaliQ's 2026 average CPC for 23 niches and seven legal practice areas for comparison only. Updated October 6, 2026.
- [Short-Form Script Pacing & Hook Timer](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/script-timer/): Times a short-form video script by retention zone (3s / 15s / 30s / 60s) and grades the hook.

## Services for Swedish companies

Copy for Originals is a one-person agency in Tidaholm, Sweden (Västra Götaland County), run by Jesse Bastide, an American copywriter and Google Ads consultant from Maine. More than SEK 20 million in managed ad spend, most of it in US lead generation. In-person meetings anywhere in Västra Götaland (for example Gothenburg, Skövde, Borås and Trollhättan) and in Stockholm; remote for businesses in the rest of Sweden. Meetings and calls are in English. Services: Google Ads for lead generation, search engine optimization (SEO) and copywriting in American English; no social media advertising or website builds at the moment. Each page below exists in English and in Swedish at its own URL.

- [Google Ads for lead generation in Sweden](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/google-ads-lead-generation-sweden/) (Swedish: [Google Ads för leadgenerering](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/sv/google-ads-leadgenerering/)): Management of Google Ads Search campaigns for Swedish businesses that get customers through inquiries (quote requests, booked meetings, phone calls), with ad copy and a landing page review. Price: 12% of ad spend per month, SEK 10,000 monthly minimum, excluding VAT, no setup fee, no lock-in; ad spend is paid directly to Google and the client owns the account with Admin access (read-only access for the first look, access to make changes once the engagement starts). First step: a free written reply naming the first thing he would change on the landing page. Explains how to stop the bleeding in a Google Ads account in six checks (search terms and negative keywords, auto-applied recommendations off, location option Presence instead of Presence or interest, Display Network and Search Partners off, only forms and calls over 60 seconds as primary conversions, pause keywords that spent 3× the allowed cost per inquiry with none), whether to clean up a messy account or start over (usually clean up), why a company doesn't show on Google, what to do about clicks without inquiries (at a 2.5% conversion rate, zero inquiries from 100 clicks is bad luck about 8% of the time; past 120 clicks it is 95% likely something is wrong), what digital marketing (digital marknadsföring) covers and which parts Copy for Originals does (search ads, SEO, landing page copy and conversion optimization; not social ads or web builds at the moment), Swedish cookie consent (Electronic Communications Act 2022:482, chapter 9 section 28, supervised by PTS; GDPR by IMY) and Google's EU user consent policy, and VAT (billed by Google Ireland Ltd, self-assessed by the Swedish company). No results guarantees and no named case studies.
- [Google Ads in the USA for Swedish companies](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/google-ads-usa-for-swedish-companies/) (Swedish: [Google Ads i USA för svenska företag](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/sv/google-ads-usa/)): Management of Google Ads Search campaigns targeting the United States for Swedish companies, with ads and landing page copy in American English. Same price: 12% of ad spend, SEK 10,000 monthly minimum, excluding VAT, no lock-in. Covers six differences from Sweden (language, geography, click prices, time zones, buyer expectations, rules), why to start in one or two states or metro areas, test budgets (minimum budget to judge a campaign = 3 × cost per click ÷ conversion rate; $5,000 to $10,000 planned for a high-competition service business), US office hours in Swedish time (Eastern 15:00–23:00, Central 16:00–24:00, Mountain 17:00–01:00, Pacific 18:00–02:00) and four ways to make sure inquiries get answered, measurement by cost per qualified inquiry with offline conversion imports, and that a Google Ads account's currency and time zone can't be changed after setup. Cites SCB (the US was Sweden's third-largest goods export market in 2025, about SEK 169 billion), Harvard Business Review on response time, and LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks ($5.42 average cost per click, $66.69 per lead). Does not include advice on US company formation, tax, customs or law.
- [English copywriting for Swedish companies selling to the US](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/english-copywriting-for-swedish-companies/) (Swedish: [Engelsk copywriting för USA](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/sv/engelsk-copywriting-usa/)): Sales copy in American English (landing pages, ads, emails, website copy, forms and buttons) written by Jesse Bastide, a native English speaker, who wrote “Love Fishing More” for Fishbrain in Stockholm in 2016. Price: a fixed quote after reading the copy; the first written reply, on what he would change first, is free. Lists eight Swedish habits in English copy and how an American reads them (for example “Welcome to contact us”, the false friends actual/aktuell and eventual/eventuell, British spellings, Swedish date and number formats, prices in kronor), the difference between translation and copywriting, five things an American buyer looks for on a Swedish supplier's page, and the FTC's truth-in-advertising and endorsement rules next to section 10 of the Swedish Marketing Act. Sweden ranks 8th of 123 in the EF English Proficiency Index 2025. Not offered: certified translation, legal texts, technical documentation, languages other than English.
- [För svenska företag](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/sv/): Swedish-language overview of the three services, a table from common problems to the right page, and the free Google Ads tools described in Swedish.

## Research

- [How much do legal marketing agencies charge? What law firm owners report paying](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/how-much-do-legal-marketing-agencies-charge/): Original research by Copy for Originals (October 2026). Fees law firm owners reported paying for their own firms in 312 coded r/LawFirm threads (October 2023 to October 2026), one figure per owner after tracing each figure to its author: SEO median $3,000 a month (14 owners, $75 to $25,000), Google Ads management median $1,175 a month with ad spend separate (4 owners, $500 to $2,500; one paid 20% of ad spend), website builds median $6,500 (4 owners, $4,000 to $20,000). Quotes owners turned down: SEO $650 to $10,000+ a month (one personal injury quote of $15,000 to $50,000 a month), websites $1,500 to $20,000. Owner-reported cost per lead: Local Services Ads about $30 to $300, Google Search ads $80 to $1,000, lead sellers $40 to $150. Includes Google’s rule that management fees be disclosed separately from Google’s exact cost, and a calculator: (agency fee + ad spend) ÷ signed cases = cost per signed case. Vendor names withheld. Data as CSV (CC BY 4.0). Educational only.
- [Local Services Ads vs Google Ads for lawyers: what changes in 2026](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/local-services-ads-vs-google-ads-for-lawyers/): Guide and calculator by Copy for Originals (October 2026), every rule taken from Google Help pages read October 6, 2026. Google is migrating Local Services Ads into Google Ads as Performance Max campaigns with pay-per-lead goals: August 2026 for select US home services, late 2026 for service-area businesses and professional services (another Google page says 2027; legal is not named), 2027 for the rest; firms get an email 14 days before. Unchanged: pay per valid lead, Search and Maps only. Changed: manual bidding and per-category targets end (one campaign-level target, so split practice areas into separate campaigns), weekly budgets become daily (weekly ÷ 7, monthly cap daily × 30.4), old performance reports do not carry over, business name and address sync from Google Business Profile, BBB callouts removed, license reverification no longer required. Credits are automatic, usually within 30 days; Google no longer credits job types or areas not served, and does not credit advice seekers, price researchers, after-hours leads or, with general lawyer leads on, any law lead. Missed calls during business hours are charged if the caller waits more than 20 seconds. In 37 r/LawFirm threads from 2023 to 2026 where lawyers described their own LSA: 30 include a lawyer for whom it worked, 10 report paying for junk leads (wrong practice area 8, free advice or can’t pay 5), 11 discuss disputes; lawyers reported about half of disputed leads credited before Google’s automated review and about 10% or less after. Owner-reported LSA cost per lead ran from about $30 (family law) to $300 (personal injury, criminal defense); one small PI firm’s cost per signed case went from $843 to $5,719 in two months. Cost per signed case = cost per lead ÷ share of real potential clients ÷ sign rate; the calculator compares LSA and Search with the firm’s own numbers and gives the break-even junk share. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Is your law firm’s Google Ads agency doing a good job? A 12-point scorecard](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/law-firm-google-ads-agency-scorecard/): Original research and an interactive scorecard by Copy for Originals (October 2026, version 2). Twelve checks a law firm owner can run in their own Google Ads account: Admin access (Admin → Access and security), the Google Ads customer ID and one account per client, ownership of domain, website, Google Business Profile, Tag Manager and call tracking numbers, the exact amount charged by Google reported separately from agency fees (Google third-party policy), spend matching Google billing, a contract that can be ended within 90 days, reports showing signed cases and cost per signed case, call tracking reconciled with the intake log, Primary conversion actions that are real leads, change history showing work in the last 30 days, approval of ads (no guarantees; ABA Model Rules 5.3 and 7.1) and a named contact. Scoring: Yes 2, Not sure 1, No 0, out of 24; a No on Admin access, customer ID or exact Google cost gives a red result; 20–24 green, 13–19 yellow, 12 or fewer red. In 312 r/LawFirm threads from October 2023 to October 2026, 188 had law firm owners describing their own experience: 63 said they paid and got no cases or no return, 57 described junk leads, 37 said their market was too expensive, 45 said doing it themselves or in-house worked better; 155 of 312 threads contained vendor promotion (open pitches, disguised praise or market research). Explains who owns a Google Ads account when an agency creates it, how to check real spend, what the Google Partner badge does and does not measure, red flags, hiring questions, and how to leave an agency without losing the account. Coded thread data as CSV (CC BY 4.0). Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Chicago personal injury lead generation: an OSINT study of 100 law firms](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/chicago-personal-injury-lead-gen-study/): Original research by Copy for Originals (October 2026) using only public sources. Of 100 Chicago personal injury firms from Google local results, 45 have Google ad creatives on record in the Ads Transparency Center and 55 have none; the largest creative volumes are national or agency-run accounts (Morgan & Morgan, TopDog Law, Lerner and Rowe, Law Tigers). Of 42 advertisers whose homepages were fetched, 20 show no call tracking and 17 no chat widget. Of 87 homepages, 84% offer a free consultation, 70% state a dollar recovery, 43% claim 24/7, 30% mention Spanish, 11% offer SMS. One-star reviews are 3.9% of 35,932 Google reviews across 94 firms; advertisers' median one-star rate is 2.9% vs 1.4% for non-advertisers. In 207 lowest-rated Google reviews at 11 firms, 38% describe no callback or an unreachable lawyer, 31% a slow case with no updates, 24% money (smaller settlement than told, fees, held check), 20% a case declined or dropped after intake; 43% got a firm response. On r/Lawyertalk, intake problems appear in 64 marketing posts vs 7 for Google Ads. Eight actions for a firm owner, each checked against Illinois Rules of Professional Conduct 7.1–7.4 (Rule 7.2 as amended July 1, 2025). Educational only, not legal advice. Data CSV (CC BY 4.0).
- [Google Ads no conversions: what 62 forum threads show](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/ppc-no-conversions-study/): Original research by Copy for Originals (October 2026). Read 121 Google Ads Community and r/PPC threads where advertisers had clicks but no conversions and coded 62. Advertisers who gave a click count had a median of 190 clicks when they asked for help; at a 2.5% expected conversion rate, 15 of 23 were past the PPC Gumball Rule red light (120 clicks). Only 3 of 62 stated a target CPA or expected conversion rate, and on the Google Ads Community only 3 of 35 stated clicks. Replies said “wait for more data” in 22 of 62 threads, including to posters with 150 to 1,179 clicks. Coded data downloadable as CSV (CC BY 4.0).
- [The PPC Gumball Rule](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/ppc-gumball-rule/): A rule of thumb named and explained by Copy for Originals (practitioners on r/PPC already use a “3× CPA” version): if a Google Ads campaign spends 3× its expected cost per conversion (3 ÷ expected conversion rate in clicks) with zero conversions, it is 95% likely that something is broken, not bad luck. Applies the statistical rule of three (Hanley and Lippman-Hand, JAMA 1983) to ad clicks. Answers “how many clicks without a conversion is normal?” by conversion rate instead of a fixed number: normal up to 2 ÷ conversion rate clicks, yellow light from 2 to 3 ÷, red light past 3 ÷ (at 2.5%: normal up to 80 clicks, red at 120; at 10%: normal up to 20, red at 30), and shows why fixed rules like “wait 100 clicks” are too early at 1% and far too late at 10%. Includes a lookup table of the chance of zero conversions by conversion rate and clicks (for example, 28% for 50 clicks at 2.5%), checkpoints at 95% and 99%, a 2× “yellow light” (after spending k× target CPA with zero conversions, the chance of bad luck is about e^−k: 37% at 1×, 13.5% at 2×, 5% at 3×, at any conversion rate) for capital preservation, a calculator and a personal injury law firm example.
- [How much should a personal injury law firm spend on Google Ads?](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/personal-injury-google-ads-budget/): Sets the minimum monthly Google Ads budget for a personal injury law firm at 3 × expected cost per lead (cost per click ÷ conversion rate), the PPC Gumball Rule checkpoint. Tables of cost per lead and minimum budget for $50–$300 cost per click and 3–10% conversion rates (for example, $6,000 a month at $100 a click and 5%), why $1,500 a month rarely works, and a calculator.
- [Google Ads for law firms: what it costs, what goes wrong, and how to tell if it’s working](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/google-ads-for-law-firms/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026) and the parent page for the law firm guides on this site. Cost: cost per lead = cost per click ÷ conversion rate, minimum monthly budget = 3 × cost per lead (at $100 a click and 5%, $2,000 a lead and $6,000 a month); LocaliQ’s 2026 average legal click is $9.87 against $5.42 across all niches, and contested keywords cost far more. The figure that 82% of law firms say Google Ads isn’t worth it comes from CallRail’s 2022 Marketing Outlook for Law Firms, a survey of 508 US law firm employees in December 2021: among firms running paid search, 82% agreed “Paid search marketing is too expensive to get good ROI”; almost 65% of respondents worked at firms with 250 to 999 employees and the most common job title was IT manager (26%); the question did not ask about tracking or signed retainers. Bidding on a competing lawyer’s name as a keyword: not allowed in North Carolina (2010 Formal Ethics Opinion 14, Rule 8.4(c)), Ohio (Opinion 2021-04) and Michigan (Opinion RI-385, without express consent); allowed with conditions in Texas (Opinion 661, July 2016), South Carolina (Ethics Advisory Opinion 20-01) and New Jersey (In re Opinion No. 735, decided May 22, 2025, with a landing-page disclaimer); Florida’s Rule 4-7.13(b)(12) turns on whether the ad misleads. Trademark cases: Lerner & Rowe v. Brown Engstrand & Shely (9th Cir. October 22, 2024, no likely confusion) and Adler v. McNeil Consultants (5th Cir. August 10, 2021, claim allowed to proceed); a Colorado suit by Franklin D. Azar & Associates settled for $1.55 million. Call recording: Google’s Local Services Ads help page says all inbound US and Canada calls through the Google forwarding number are recorded after a pre-recorded notice, and Google Ads Help says the call recording setting is now enabled by default (off for healthcare and financial services; legal services not named). North Carolina proposed barring lawyers from Local Services Ads in 2021 and withdrew the proposal in April 2022. Intake: in Clio’s 2024 secret-shopper test 33% of firms answered email and 48% neither answered the phone nor called back; in 207 lowest-rated reviews at 11 Chicago injury firms, 38% describe no callback. Working test: cost per signed case = (ad spend + agency fee) ÷ signed cases; zero conversions after 3 ÷ conversion rate clicks (120 at 2.5%) is under 5% likely to be luck. Sources read October 13, 2026. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Can a law firm bid on a competitor’s name in Google Ads? The rules by state](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/can-lawyers-bid-on-competitor-names-google-ads/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026) to lawyers bidding on a competing lawyer’s name as a search keyword (competitive keyword advertising). Seven states have a published position. Not allowed: North Carolina (2010 Formal Ethics Opinion 14, adopted April 27, 2012: “it is a violation of Rule 8.4(c) for a lawyer to select another lawyer’s name to be used in his own keyword advertising”; 2023 Formal Ethics Opinion 4, adopted January 19, 2024, extends this to a unique firm trade name but not a generic phrase such as “Durham family lawyers”); Ohio (Board of Professional Conduct Opinion 2021-04, June 11, 2021, nonbinding advisory: “A lawyer or law firm may not purchase the name of another lawyer or law firm for use in competitive keyword online advertising”); Michigan (State Bar Opinion RI-385, November 18, 2022: not without the other lawyer’s express consent). Allowed with conditions: Texas (Opinion 661, July 2016: the ad must not be false or misleading or suggest affiliation); South Carolina (Ethics Advisory Opinion 20-01: no derogatory or uncivil message, no disguised redirect link); New Jersey (Supreme Court, In re Opinion No. 735, decided May 22, 2025: buying a competitor’s name as a keyword “does not, in itself, constitute a violation of the RPCs,” but the landing page must carry the disclaimer “You arrived at this page via a paid advertisement on [insert name of search engine provider] through paid keyword search results. This website and the legal business it describes are affiliated only with [insert name of purchasing attorney] and the other attorneys referenced within this website.”). Florida: Rule 4-7.13(b)(12), effective May 2, 2022 (case SC20-1467, March 3, 2022), prohibits ads that mislead a person searching for one lawyer into unknowingly contacting another; the comment says the triggered ad is not misleading if the first text displayed is the advertising lawyer’s or firm’s name. Court cases: Lerner & Rowe v. Brown Engstrand & Shely (9th Cir. October 22, 2024): no likely confusion; 236 calls mentioning Lerner & Rowe were 0.216% of 109,322 ad impressions; 7,452 clicks (6.82%). Adler v. McNeil Consultants (5th Cir. August 10, 2021): dismissal reversed because the complaint alleged generic click-to-call ads and misleading call handling “beyond the mere purchase of trademarks as keywords.” Habush v. Cannon (Wis. Ct. App. February 21, 2013): no violation of Wisconsin’s privacy statute. Franklin D. Azar & Associates settled a 2022 suit against an Alabama firm for $1.55 million. Google’s Trademarks policy will not restrict “Using trademarks as keywords” but will restrict a trademark in a direct competitor’s ad text after a complaint. Also covers how broad and phrase match can show an ad on a competitor’s name without the firm choosing it, a six-point check before bidding, and six steps for a firm whose name is being bid on (auction insights lists the advertisers in the same auctions). Sources read October 13, 2026. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Personal injury Google Ads: what it costs, who you’re bidding against, and where cases get lost](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/personal-injury-google-ads/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026) for personal injury law firms, built on its own studies. Google Ads work for a personal injury firm when the monthly budget is at least 3 × expected cost per lead, the firm counts signed cases, and every ad call is answered or returned. Cost: cost per lead = cost per click ÷ conversion rate; at $100 a click and 5%, $2,000 a lead and a $6,000 minimum monthly budget ($12,000 at $200 a click); $1,500 a month at $100 a click buys 15 clicks with about a 46% chance of zero leads; LocaliQ’s average for Accidents & Personal Injury is $9.30 a click (April 2022 to March 2023) while owners on r/LawFirm cite injury clicks of $200 or more. Competition: 45 of 100 visible Chicago injury firms have Google ad creatives on record and eight hold most of the volume (the four largest are Morgan & Morgan, TopDog Law, Lerner and Rowe and Law Tigers). Setup: one ad group for one case type, 5 to 20 phrase and exact match keywords, location set to Presence, calls of 60 seconds or more counted as leads, pause a keyword after it spends twice the target cost per lead with no conversions. Starter negative keywords by searcher type (job, education, do-it-yourself, case types not taken, other firms’ names where the state prohibits bidding on them). Local Services Ads: owner-reported injury leads about $300; one firm’s cost per signed case went from $843 to $5,719 in two months. What 87 Chicago injury sites say: free consultation 84%, dollar recovery 70%, 24/7 43%, no fee 43%, Spanish 30%, reviews widget 14%, text option 11%. Intake: 38% of 207 lowest-rated reviews at 11 firms describe no callback; 20 of 42 advertisers show no call tracking; 74 of 100 firms list 24-hour opening and about half their sites repeat it. Clicks without a lead: normal up to 2 ÷ conversion rate, probably broken past 3 ÷ conversion rate (40 and 60 clicks at 5%). Measure by cost per signed case = (ad spend + agency fee) ÷ signed cases, because contingency fees arrive months or years later. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Do 82% of law firms say Google Ads isn’t worth it? The statistic traced to its source](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/82-percent-law-firms-paid-search-roi/): Claim check by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026). The figure comes from CallRail’s “2022 Marketing Outlook for Law Firms,” a survey of 508 US law firm employees conducted in December 2021. Under “Law firms that engage in paid search marketing say the following,” 82% agreed, 16% disagreed and 2% answered don’t know to “Paid search marketing is too expensive to get good ROI.” The 82% is a share of firms already running paid search, not of all law firms, and the companion 78% is a share of firms whose clients find them through search. Respondents by firm size: 1 to 19 employees 3%, 20 to 99 14%, 100 to 249 18%, 250 to 499 30%, 500 to 999 35%; most common job titles IT manager (26%) and law firm partner (16%). The survey did not ask whether paid search works or about tracking signed cases; a separate finding in the same report says 82% of firms use single-touch attribution. CallRail’s later reports: October 2022 survey of 600 respondents, “97% of law firms who use PPC say paid search is too expensive to get good ROI”; December 2024 survey of 49 respondents, “25% of law firms believe paid search marketing is too expensive to get a good return on investment” (90% were spending on PPC, 42% wanted to spend more); October 2025 survey of 100, statement not reported, 47% named paid search as a channel driving new business. The samples differ, so the numbers are not a trend. The report’s own callout, “78% of firms use paid search marketing, but 82% don’t think the ROI is worth it,” drops both conditions. Four later versions are quoted: HawkSEM (2023), Practice Proof’s 2026 benchmarks (no year given), Whitehat SEO (restated as UK law firms, no source) and WhatConverts (headline “82% Don’t Think It Works”). Suggested citation: in a December 2021 CallRail survey of 508 US law firm employees, 82% of firms running paid search agreed it was “too expensive to get good ROI”; a December 2024 CallRail survey of 49 respondents put the figure at 25%. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Personal injury lawyer leads: buy them or generate your own?](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/personal-injury-lawyer-leads/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026), built on its open data from r/LawFirm threads (October 2023 to October 2026). Compare lead sources by cost per signed case = cost per lead ÷ share of leads that are real potential clients ÷ share of those that sign (a $100 lead where one in five is real and one in four signs costs $2,000 per signed case). Owner-reported prices: bought leads $40 to $150 each across practice areas; personal injury Local Services Ads leads about $220 to $300; Google Search ads leads $80 to $1,000; two injury firms paid lead vendors $8,000 to $10,000 a month; one was quoted $1,500 per “qualified” car accident call (about $3,000 a signed case at the vendor’s claimed 40% to 60% signing rate). Bought-lead outcomes reported by personal injury owners: 20 leads, one signed case; 8 marketplace leads, none reachable; $10,000 a month, worth it but smaller cases. Of 188 threads where owners described their own paid marketing, 20 were about a lead vendor: 15 described junk leads, 7 paid and got no cases or no return, 3 said leads were shared with other firms, 4 mentioned a vendor tactic that might break a rule. One injury firm’s Local Services Ads: December 2024 $23,188 and 16 signed ($1,449 a case); February 2025 $18,544, 85 leads, 22 signed ($843); April 2025 $11,440, 52 leads, 2 signed ($5,719); cost per lead stayed near $220 while the share signing fell from 26% to 4%. ABA Model Rule 7.2 Comment 5: a lawyer may pay others for generating client leads as long as the lead generator does not recommend the lawyer, payment is consistent with Rules 1.5(e) and 5.4, and its communications are consistent with Rule 7.1. Six questions for a lead vendor (exclusive or shared, how generated, bad-lead credits, contract length, original inquiry, signed cases per hundred leads). Intake: in CallRail’s December 2024 survey (49 respondents) 96% said slow or no response can lose cases, and 28% of calls to law firms in CallRail’s data were missed. Copy for Originals manages Google Ads and does not sell leads. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Five short answers for law firm Search campaigns](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/law-firm-google-ads-faq/): Good conversion rate (cost per click ÷ target cost per lead), conversions needed for Target CPA (Google recommends at least 30), broad match for law firms, starter negative keywords, and Maximize conversions vs Target CPA.
- [Does Google record calls to law firms from its ads?](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/does-google-record-calls-to-law-firms/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026), quoting Google’s help pages as read that day. Yes, in the United States and Canada, when the call goes through a Google forwarding number. Local Services Ads: “all inbound calls from customers via the Google forwarding number are recorded by Google”; customers are notified by a pre-recorded message; “Recordings and messages in legal verticals are retained for 60 days” (up to 180 days in other categories); Google reviews recordings “on a limited basis” for billing disputes, billing, policy enforcement, spam detection, feedback, product improvement and monitoring; recordings are not available for health care categories or tax specialists; the help pages describe no setting to turn recording off. Google Ads: “The call recording setting is now enabled by default to allow for AI-powered lead qualification”; it applies to calls to call ads and call assets and from website visits through a Google forwarding number with call reporting on; it stays off for advertisers who turned it off earlier and for healthcare and financial services (legal services are not named); Google’s AI evaluates every recorded call and shows an AI-generated summary and hashtags in call reports; recordings play for 30 days and cannot be downloaded; Admin and Standard users, including manager accounts with Admin access, can play them. Turn it off under Admin, Account settings, Call ads, Call recording; conversions then fall back to call duration. Turning off call reporting shows the firm’s own number and stops Google tracking calls. Google’s Call Ads Supplemental Terms say the advertiser has given notice to, and has the express consent of, its agents and employees. Ethics: no state opinion found says recording breaches confidentiality. North Carolina’s Proposed 2021 Formal Ethics Opinion 5 would have barred participation under Rule 8.4(d) and was withdrawn in April 2022 after the committee concluded the recordings “are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosures”; the State Bar Journal article reminds lawyers to investigate any advertising program and to warn callers that a first call creates no client-lawyer relationship and is not confidential or privileged. Wisconsin’s State Bar ethics counsel wrote in January 2021 that it depends on whether the caller is a prospective client. ABA Model Rule 1.18(b) is quoted. Includes a seven-step list for a firm. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [How does a law firm track signed cases back to Google Ads clicks?](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/track-signed-cases-google-ads/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026), from Google’s help pages as read that day. A law firm imports signed cases into Google Ads as offline conversions: it stores the Google click ID (GCLID) with each lead and, when the lead signs, uploads the click ID with a conversion name and the date and time. “Google Click ID (GCLID) is a URL parameter passed with ad clicks”; it requires auto-tagging and is case sensitive. Five setup steps: turn on auto-tagging; capture the click ID on every form with a hidden field; store it with the lead in the intake system; create an offline conversion action (Goals, Summary, create conversion action, offline); upload regularly through Google Ads Data Manager (Google Sheets, file stores, Salesforce, HubSpot). From June 15, 2026 uploads moved to the Data Manager API. Time limit: offline conversions “uploaded more than 90 days after the associated last click won’t be imported,” 63 days for enhanced conversions for leads; a settlement that arrives later cannot be imported, so import the signed case with an estimated value. Calls: Google’s call conversion import matches on the caller’s phone number and call start time and requires Google forwarding numbers; the alternative is a call tracking service that ties the call to the click ID. What Google receives: a click ID import sends the click ID, conversion name, date and time and an optional value, none of which identifies the client; enhanced conversions for leads, which Google now recommends (“a median 10% increase in conversions”), also sends hashed contact details such as an email address; the call import sends the caller’s phone number. Keep the conversion name neutral (“Signed case”), use one estimated value per practice area, and add nothing else. ABA Model Rule 1.6(c) is quoted. Bidding: Google recommends judging Target CPA over at least 30 conversions in 30 days, so a firm signing fewer cases than that can keep signed cases as a secondary (observation-only) conversion and bid on leads. In 9 of 188 r/LawFirm owner threads the owner could not tell which leads came from where. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Lead generation for lawyers: what works, what it costs, and where leads get lost](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/lead-generation-for-lawyers/): Guide by Copy for Originals (October 13, 2026) for any practice area, built on its open data from r/LawFirm (October 2023 to October 2026). Lead generation for lawyers (attorney lead generation, law firm lead generation) has six sources: referrals, organic search and Google Business Profile, Google Search ads, Local Services Ads, social media ads and bought leads. Owner complaints by main channel in 188 threads where owners described their own paid marketing: lead vendors, 20 threads, 15 junk leads, 7 paid with no cases or no return; Local Services Ads, 19 threads, 13 and 7; Google Search ads, 13 threads, 5 and 2; SEO, 39 threads, 4 and 17; several channels, 83 threads, 18 and 25. Pay-per-lead channels draw junk-lead complaints; monthly SEO fees draw no-return complaints. Owner-reported cost per lead: Local Services Ads about $30 to $300, Google Search ads $80 to $1,000, bought leads $40 to $150; SEO median $3,000 a month (14 owners). Bought lawyer leads: in the 20 lead vendor threads, 3 owners said leads were also sold to other firms; satisfied owners had a follow-up system and a count of results. ABA Model Rule 7.2 Comment 5 allows paying for leads if the lead generator does not recommend the lawyer. Spend ranged from a few hundred dollars a month to $50,000 or more; measure by cost per signed case = (spend on the source + fees) ÷ signed cases. In 45 of 188 threads owners said doing marketing themselves or in-house worked better, mostly content and SEO; in 12 the firm’s own intake was the problem; in 9 the owner could not tell which leads came from where. Intake: Clio’s 2024 secret-shopper test found 33% of firms answered email and 48% neither answered the phone nor called back; CallRail’s October 2025 survey of 100 legal professionals named SEO (54%), video (50%), paid search (47%), paid social (38%) and content (37%) as channels driving new business. Copy for Originals manages Google Ads and does not sell leads. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Why healthcare PPC experience transfers to law firm Google Ads](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/healthcare-ppc-for-law-firms/): Compares a healthcare practice’s Google Ads account with a law firm’s: few expensive leads, phone calls as the lead, the real result recorded offline (booked patient vs signed retainer), sensitive inquiries (HIPAA vs client confidentiality), regulated ad copy (healthcare policies vs state bar rules based on ABA Model Rule 7.1) and urgent local searches. Explains why offline conversion imports of signed cases and click-ID-only tracking carry over, and what doesn’t: practice-area knowledge, higher legal CPCs, lead-gen competitors, delayed contingency fees and state-by-state rules.
- [How to write content that LLMs retrieve and cite](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/rag-friendly-content/): An evidence-rated guide to answer engine optimization (AEO) and RAG-friendly content, with sources and a 12-point checklist.
- [HIPAA-compliant conversion tracking for Google Ads](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/hipaa-google-ads-conversions/): Compares the options a healthcare practice has for tracking Google Ads conversions without sending PHI to Google (Google signs no BAA for Google Ads): healthcare tracking platforms (Curve, Ours Privacy, Freshpaint), enterprise CDPs with a BAA tier (Piwik PRO, Segment, RudderStack, Tealium), server-side Google Tag Manager on a BAA-covered host (Google Cloud Run, Stape Custom), free click-ID-only offline conversion imports, and HIPAA call tracking (CallRail, CallTrackingMetrics, Invoca). Gives prices labeled by source, setup effort and fit for practices without IT staff, a section on what could not be verified, and Manual CPC judged by new-patient growth as an alternative. Sources accessed October 5, 2026. Educational only, not legal advice.
- [Should AI fully manage your Google Ads campaigns?](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/should-ai-manage-google-ads/): Weighs the pros and cons of letting Google’s automation (auto-applied recommendations, AI Max for Search, Smart Bidding without a target) or AI agents from Anthropic, OpenAI and others manage Google Ads lead gen Search campaigns. Concludes that AI suggests and a person approves: Smart Bidding works for hitting a target CPA or ROAS with enough conversion data (Google recommends at least 30 conversions to judge Target CPA; broad match needs at least 50 a month in our experience), while AI agents are best at research, analysis and building deterministic tools. Cites Google Help, Anthropic and OpenAI guidance, SMEC’s AI Max study and the State of PPC 2026 survey, checked October 5, 2026.
- [Speaking rate study of top YouTube Shorts](https://tools.copyfororiginals.com/script-timer/study/): Speaking rate and hook length measured in 132 top YouTube Shorts.
